market_context: United States and general English-speaking market
title: Ricotta vs. mozzarella: nutrition differences

seo.title: Ricotta vs. mozzarella: protein, fat and calories
seo.meta_description: Ricotta and mozzarella are both fresh cheeses, but mozzarella is usually much more protein-dense. Compare equal weights and see why moisture changes the numbers.

excerpt: USDA whole-milk ricotta provides about 157 calories, 7.8 g protein and 11 g fat per 100 g. A whole-milk mozzarella reference is around 300 calories, 22 g protein and 22 g fat. Mozzarella is much more concentrated, although very fresh high-moisture mozzarella can be substantially lighter than that reference.
content_html:
Ricotta and mozzarella can share the same lasagna, but nutritionally they occupy different spaces. Moisture is a major reason. Ricotta is very wet; many mozzarella products are much more concentrated.

Equal 100 g comparison

Whole-milk ricottaWhole-milk mozzarella reference
Calories~157~300
Protein~7.8 g~22.2 g
Fat~11 g~22.4 g
Calcium~200 mg~500 mg

The mozzarella reference contains nearly three times as much protein per 100 g.

Not all mozzarella has 300 calories

Fresh mozzarella packed in liquid retains more water and can have substantially fewer calories per 100 g. Low-moisture mozzarella used on pizza is denser. The product's moisture and milkfat level matter as much as the word mozzarella.

They are made differently

Traditional ricotta recovers proteins from whey left after cheesemaking, although commercial ricotta can include milk and cream. Mozzarella is made from curd that is heated and stretched in the pasta-filata process.

Italian cooking uses them differently for a reason

Ricotta is moist, granular and relatively soft; mozzarella forms an elastic curd that melts and stretches. Those properties come from different processes and protein structures, which is why substituting one for the other changes more than calories.

In lasagna, fillings or desserts, ricotta adds bulk and creaminess. On pizza or gratins, mozzarella provides melt and stretch. The nutrition table explains the contrast, but culinary function often decides which cheese actually makes sense.

What about a 50 g portion?

Using the references above, 50 g provides roughly 79 calories and 3.9 g protein from ricotta versus 150 calories and 11 g protein from mozzarella.

Ricotta is useful for creamy volume; mozzarella is usually far more protein- and calcium-dense by weight.

faq.question: Which has more protein, ricotta or mozzarella?
faq.answer: Mozzarella in these references: about 22 g/100 g versus 7.8 g for whole-milk ricotta.

faq.question: Which has fewer calories?
faq.answer: The ricotta reference: about 157 versus 300 calories/100 g.

faq.question: Does all mozzarella have 300 calories per 100 g?
faq.answer: No. High-moisture fresh mozzarella can be much lower; low-moisture types are more concentrated.

faq.question: Are ricotta and mozzarella made the same way?
faq.answer: No. Ricotta is traditionally whey-based, while mozzarella is a stretched-curd cheese.
